channel.title: Food Safety Magazine - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Food Safety Magazine (food-safety.com)

item.title: Study Identifies Critical Temperature Threshold During Food Processing to Inactivate Norovirus
item.description: Maximum reductions in norovirus infectivity occurred rapidly once temperatures reached 60 °C (140 °F). The findings could help inform improved thermal processing recommendations for foodborne norovirus.

item.title: FoodSafe Drains Launches Drainage Evaluation Program for Food Facilities
item.description: The engineering-led assessment program helps food and beverage processors identify drainage risks, prioritize hygienic upgrades, and implement facility-specific standard operating procedures (SOPs) for long-term performance.

item.title: Hillbrush Transitions Hygiene Range to Plastic Free Packaging Amid Rising PFAS Restrictions
item.description: Hillbrush Transitions Hygiene Range to Plastic Free Packaging Amid Rising PFAS Restrictions

item.title: FDA Releases Initial Findings from Foodborne Pathogen Study in California Growing Region
item.description: The California Longitudinal Study, a five-year environmental study of California’s Central Coast produce-growing region, identified wildlife, livestock, and surface water as potential contributors to the persistence and movement of Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli (STEC).

item.title: Critical Implications of Hygienic Zoning for Food and Beverage Processing
item.description: This article presents the conceptual understanding and objectives of hygienic zoning for food and beverage processing facilities. It discusses linear workflow and cross-contamination, the design of cleaning and disinfection strategies, pathogen environmental monitoring, and the legal implications of hygienic zoning and positive outcomes for industry.

item.title: Study Shows Drinking Water Quality Significantly Impacts Salmonella Vaccines for Poultry
item.description: Elevated levels of certain metals and the presence of commonly used disinfectants were found to inactivate Salmonella vaccines administered to poultry via drinking water.

item.title: FDA Redacts All Key Details in Summary of Fatal Listeriosis Outbreak Linked to Produce
item.description: Despite having Listeria-positive samples that matched the outbreak strain via whole genome sequencing (WGS), which prompted an FDA Import Alert and a company recall for the suspected vehicle of illness, FDA did not disclose the specific product or any of the firms implicated.

item.title: Report Raises Concerns About Microplastics, Chemicals Released by Microwavable Meals
item.description: A literature review conducted by Greenpeace concluded that heating food in plastic packaging—even ready-to-heat meals labeled as “microwave-safe” or “oven-safe”—may significantly increase the migration of microplastics and chemical additives into food.

item.title: Catalyst Food Leaders’ 2026 Virtual Summit to Focus on ‘Reimagining Leadership’
item.description: Registration is now open for the half-day event, taking place on April 8 and designed for food manufacturing and food safety leaders.

item.title: Ep. 213. Richard Stier: Driving Continuous Improvement in Food Safety and Sanitation
item.description: In this episode of Food Safety Matters, Richard Stier, M.S., a consulting food scientist and longtime Food Safety Magazine contributor, recalls lessons from decades in food processing facilities, discussing crisis preparedness, internal audits, facility sanitation and employee hygiene, HACCP, and why strong food safety programs must be continuously improved to remain effective.
